source.title: Reexamining the principle of mean-variance preservation for neural network initialization

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Compares data-dependent initialization schemes and batch normalization, then reports their effects on training speed in two convolutional networks.
record.gate_note: The study reports preactivation statistics and training-speed comparisons. Preactivation statistics are not training classification error results; the training curves are figure-only. It does not test the cited results from other work.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares training speed with and without batch normalization in two additional network/task settings, testing V6. It is not an original source for that version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's training-speed summary is accurate but incomplete. The authors also conclude that preserving total mean and variance does not preserve sample statistics in deep ReLU networks. Sample-centering initialization improves training speed, and batch normalization improves it further, suggesting that initialization contributes to part of batch normalization's speedup.
record.recipe_differences: Uses one-time data-dependent total and sample mean-variance initialization and compares them with batch normalization; it does not reproduce the versions' specified initialization or network recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-speed comparisons vary by task and network: object recognition with ALL-CNN-C and segmentation with UNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Sample initialization improved training speed over total initialization in both tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Centering sample preactivations and rescaling their variance at initialization speeds training relative to preserving total preactivation variance in the tested networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Kaiming-initialized ReLU networks preserve total preactivation variance while sample variance declines with depth; for normalized or independent-component inputs it tends to zero in the wide-network analysis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserving variance across random networks does not ensure preservation of variance across inputs within a fixed deep ReLU network.

record.problems: Training-speed values are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. Results are based on three randomly initialized runs; standard deviations are described as generally too small to see. Learning rates were selected optimally for each setting, and exact learning rates are referred to supplemental material not supplied here.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted labels, model-size effects, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student local minima and additional student neurons.
Training-error degradation with increasing depth and controlled comparisons of plain networks with identity residual shortcuts.

Activation-matched initialization improving training through preserved signal and gradient propagation; greater trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian weights; very deep tanh and convolutional networks.
Stability thresholds, loss transients, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability training, and divergence.
The original sigmoid/MNIST, VGG/CIFAR-10, and Inception/ImageNet settings; maximum stable learning rates; Fixup training without normalization.

missing.what: The optimal learning rate was larger for batch-normalized and sample-initialized networks than for total-initialized networks. This bears on V6's learning-rate component, but an optimal rate is not a measured maximum stable rate; no numerical rates are supplied.
missing.locator: Section V, paragraph describing SGD settings and learning-rate selection; rates referred to Supplemental Material.

record.verdict_notes: Use the explicit textual training-speed comparisons without reconstructing figure values. Neither the preactivation-statistics analysis nor the initialization-only comparisons directly establish V4's specified training mechanism. Larger optimized learning rates alone do not establish higher stability limits.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and early stopping.
Teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of student width.
Depth-related training error and residual shortcuts; the text describes UNet skip connections but does not compare them with a plain network.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation as a determinant of trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initializations.
Training above a stability limit, loss increases, curvature or sharpness changes, and divergence.
The reported experiments use ALL-CNN-C and UNet, not the version's specified sigmoid MNIST, VGG CIFAR-10, or Inception ImageNet settings. Fixup is not tested.
